paragraphs: Rabbi Yusta, son of Rabbi Simon.

In Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin, chapter 6, at the supplied halakhah label ה״ל [compare 6:4], he reports in Rabbi Baitos's name. Also mentioned at the beginning of Shekalim chapter 2; perhaps he is the one called R' Yose, son of R' Simon, in Maaser Sheni 4:2.

notes.text: בש״ר means “in the name of Rabbi,” not a person Bashr. The Eruvin halakhah letter ל remains unresolved. The possible Yusta/Yose identification is Hyman’s.

The saved whole Venice Eruvin6 halakhah4 scalar has Yusti bei Rabbi Simon in Rabbi Baitos’s name; whole Shekalim2:1 scalar has Yusta bei Rabbi Simon. These matching passages supersede the earlier exact-spelling nonmatch, without proving the printed ה״ל was a misread ד. Supplied ה״ל remains beside6:4. MaaserSheni4:2 and the possible Yusta/Yose identity remain Hyman’s conjecture and were not newly inspected. בש״ר is reporting in Rabbi’s name, not a person Bashr. Full Rabbi titles are scoped to the actually matched names; the uninspected Yose occurrence stays abbreviated.

Hyman’s printed page 704 does give ה״ל. In the Venice text of Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 6:4, Yusti son of Rabbi Simon speaks in Rabbi Baitos’s name. The Venice text of Shekalim 2:1 names Yusta son of Rabbi Simon. In Guggenheimer’s Maaser Sheni 4:2, Yose son of Rabbi Simon speaks in Rabbi Yochanan’s name. Whether Yusta and Yose are the same person remains Hyman’s conjecture.
